taxonomy:
Here is a taxonomy of the listed grid-based logic games, using only the rule descriptions provided.

## 1. Loop-drawing puzzles
These require drawing one continuous loop through cells or dots.

- **Dotchi-Loop** — single loop through cell centers; must pass white circles and avoid black circles.
- **Masyu** — single loop through cell centers; passes through black and white circles with turn/straight constraints.
- **Mid-loop** — single loop through cells; must pass through all black circles as midpoints of straight segments.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — single loop through cells; must visit rooms in an alternating moon/sun pattern.
- **Nagareru** — single directional loop; arrows determine the loop’s direction and wind affects movement.
- **Slitherlink** — single loop on dot grid; numbers indicate how many lines surround a cell.
- **Suraromu** — single loop through cells; must pass all gates in order constraints from numbered circle.
- **Yajilin** — single loop through cells; numbers indicate black cells in arrow direction.
- **Numberlink** — connect matching number pairs with non-crossing lines.
- **Pencils** — draw lines from pencil tips; lines follow pencil lengths and cannot branch or cross.

## 2. Shading / coloring puzzles
These ask you to color cells black/white or shaded/unshaded under structural constraints.

- **Akari** — place light bulbs in white cells so all white cells are illuminated.
- **Hitori** — blacken cells so numbers don’t repeat in rows/columns; black cells don’t touch; white cells stay connected.
- **Kurodoko** — blacken cells so numbered cells see the correct number of white cells; black cells don’t touch; white cells connected.
- **Kurotto** — color cells so circles count the total continuous black cells extending from them.
- **Nurikabe** — blacken cells to form one continuous wall; white areas are numbered islands.
- **Norinori** — place blocks in pairs in consecutive black squares; each bold region has two black squares.
- **Nurimeizu** — paint cells to create a maze from S to G with room-based constraints.
- **Nurimisaki** — fill cells so circles remain white “Misaki” cells with straight-line counts; white cells connected.
- **Shakashaka** — place black triangles in squares so remaining white parts form rectangles/squares.
- **Sto-stone** — fill colored cells so room black-cell counts match and dropped stones fill the bottom half.
- **Usowan** — color cells so each region has exactly one wrong number and colored cells obey adjacency rules.
- **Tilepaint** — color tiles so diagonal-number clues determine black-cell counts to the right/down.
- **Double Choco** — divide grid into blocks containing matching white/gray areas.
- **Nuritwin** — shade cells so each region contains exactly two same-sized blocks.
- **Choco Banana** — divide grid into blocks with matching white and gray areas of same form.
- **Five Cells** — divide grid into blocks of exactly five cells.
- **Chained Block** — fill cells into black-cell blocks with size/shape uniqueness constraints in chains.
- **Evolomino** — place squares in blocks that grow by one square along arrow routes.
- **Sashigane** — divide grid into L-shaped blocks with arrows/open circles defining bends and ends.
- **Shikaku** — divide grid into rectangles, each containing exactly one number.
- **Fillomino** — divide grid into blocks of equal numbers, each block size matching the number.
- **Ripple Effect** — fill rooms with consecutive numbers starting from 1, with spacing rules for duplicates.
- **Sudoku** — fill cells with 1–9 so each row, column, and 3×3 block contains all digits.
- **Makaro** — fill rooms with numbers; arrows point to the largest adjacent number.
- **Nansuke** — fill blank cells with numbers from a given list, arranged vertically or horizontally.
- **Juosan** — fill cells with horizontal or vertical marks under territory count constraints.

## 3. Connectivity / island / bridge puzzles
These involve linking separated objects or maintaining connected regions.

- **Hashiwokakero** — connect numbered islands with bridges matching island counts.
- **Satogaeri** — move circles so each country contains one circle; tracks cannot cross.
- **Yosenabe** — move circles into gray areas; gray-area sums must match circle values.
- **Numberlink** — connect pairs of identical numbers with continuous lines.
- **Nurikabe** — white numbered islands separated by black wall.
- **Hitori** — white cells must remain connected.
- **Kurodoko** — white cells must remain connected.
- **Norinori** — black squares are grouped in pairs within regions.
- **Nuritwin** — shaded cells must connect across region boundaries.
- **Sto-stone** — stones “drop” to fill bottom half, with room constraints.

## 4. Region partitioning puzzles
These focus on dividing the grid into rooms, blocks, territories, or tiles.

- **Choco Banana** — divide into blocks with paired white/gray shapes.
- **Double Choco** — divide into blocks with paired white/gray shapes.
- **Five Cells** — divide into blocks of five cells.
- **Fillomino** — divide into blocks of equal numbers.
- **Shikaku** — divide into rectangles.
- **Sashigane** — divide into L-shaped blocks.
- **Nuritwin** — divide into regions each containing two blocks.
- **Chained Block** — identify blocks and chains of blocks.
- **Heyawake** — rooms are predefined; shading must obey room and line constraints.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — rooms constrain loop traversal.
- **Ripple Effect** — rooms constrain number placement.
- **Makaro** — rooms constrain number placement.
- **Sto-stone** — rooms constrain black-cell counts.
- **Juosan** — territories constrain mark counts.
- **Tilepaint** — tiles constrain coloring.
- **Usowan** — rectangles constrain one wrong number.
- **Nurimeizu** — rooms constrain painting and maze behavior.

## 5. Number-placement puzzles
These are primarily about placing numbers according to local/global constraints.

- **Sudoku** — place digits 1–9 in rows, columns, and blocks.
- **Fillomino** — fill blocks with numbers matching block size.
- **Ripple Effect** — fill rooms with consecutive numbers and spacing rules.
- **Makaro** — fill rooms with numbers 1..n and arrow constraints.
- **Nansuke** — fill blanks with numbers from a list.
- **Juosan** — fill with horizontal/vertical marks, with territory counts.
- **Usowan** — numbers indicate adjacent colored cells, with one wrong number per region.
- **Kurodoko** — numbers indicate visible white-cell counts.
- **Kurotto** — circles indicate sums of continuous black cells.
- **Hashiwokakero** — island numbers indicate bridge counts.
- **Nurimisaki** — circle numbers indicate straight white-cell lengths.
- **Satogaeri** — circle numbers indicate movement distance.
- **Yosenabe** — gray-area numbers indicate sum of entering circles.
- **Makaro** — room numbers and arrow comparisons.
- **Shakashaka** — numbers indicate surrounding black triangles.
- **Slitherlink** — numbers indicate surrounding line counts.
- **Akari** — numbers indicate adjacent bulbs.
- **Hebi** — black-cell arrows indicate nearest snake number.
- **Suraromu** — open circle number indicates gates to pass.
- **Pencils** — pencil numbers indicate pencil length.
- **Dotchi-Loop / Masyu / Mid-loop / Yajilin / Nagareru** — circle/arrow clues constrain loop behavior.

## 6. Shape / pattern / polyomino puzzles
These emphasize specific shapes or shape matching.

- **Chained Block** — blocks have size and shape uniqueness in chains.
- **Double Choco** — paired areas must match in form.
- **Choco Banana** — paired areas must match in form.
- **Evolomino** — blocks grow by adding one square without rotating/flipping.
- **LITS** — tetrominoes in rooms; same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch.
- **Sashigane** — all blocks are L-shaped.
- **Shakashaka** — triangles in squares create rectangular white regions.
- **Five Cells** — blocks must contain exactly five cells.
- **Shikaku** — blocks are rectangles.
- **Nuritwin** — each region contains exactly two same-sized blocks.
- **Norinori** — blocks in twos in black squares.
- **Sto-stone** — stones drop to fill bottom half.

## 7. Snake / path / directional puzzles
These involve ordered paths, directional movement, or snake-like structures.

- **Hebi** — snakes numbered 1 to 5 must connect sequentially.
- **Nagareru** — loop direction is governed by arrows and wind.
- **Pencils** — lines extend from pencil tips through pencil lengths.
- **Satogaeri** — circles move along tracks into countries.
- **Yosenabe** — circles move into gray areas via arrows.
- **Suraromu** — loop must pass gates in a specified order.
- **Masyu** — loop turns/straightens around circles.
- **Dotchi-Loop** — loop behavior depends on circle type.
- **Mid-loop** — loop passes through black circles as straight midpoints.

## 8. Adjacency / non-adjacency constraint puzzles
These are defined mainly by what may or may not touch.

- **Hitori** — black cells never touch.
- **Kurodoko** — black cells never touch.
- **Nurikabe** — black cells form a continuous wall, no 2×2 black.
- **LITS** — same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch except at corners.
- **Nurimisaki** — no 2×2 or larger same-color groups.
- **Nuritwin** — two blocks in a region must not touch; no 2×2 all shaded.
- **Shakashaka** — white remainder must be rectangular/square.
- **Usowan** — colored cells cannot touch; white cells must stay connected.
- **Heyawake** — painted cells cannot touch; white cells must remain connected.
- **Akari** — bulbs cannot illuminate each other.
- **Hashiwokakero** — bridges cannot cross.
- **Numberlink** — lines cannot cross or branch.
- **Slitherlink** — loop cannot cross or branch.
- **Masyu** — loop cannot cross or branch.
- **Yajilin** — loop cannot cross or branch; black cells cannot touch.
- **Nagareru** — loop cannot cross or branch; wind blocks movement.
- **Pencils** — pencil lines cannot cross or branch.
